content_note: Every rule here is intent-only: a name, an id and a logic line that names the detections the rule would join. There is no query, schedule, severity or alert mapping, so nothing in this file can be imported into a tenant as-is. Author the rule in the XSIAM console from the logic line.

rules.logic: XQL(EMAIL-005 AiTM Look-Alike Click Permitted) FOLLOWED_BY XQL(EMAIL-005 Session-Cookie Replay Sign-In from New ASN) FOLLOWED_BY XQL(EMAIL-005 Compromised-Mailbox Finance-Mail Reconnaissance) — joined on user_principal within a 60-minute window. The permitted click to an AiTM look-alike domain plus the token-replay sign-in from a new ASN name the Meddler-in-the-Middle compromise; fusing them with post-compromise finance-mail reconnaissance on the same mailbox raises ONE account-takeover incident. The mailbox-access events are routine activity in isolation, so it is their co-occurrence with the AiTM click and the new-ASN token-replay sign-in on the same user_principal that classifies the takeover. The AiTM domain and the anomalous ASN attach as incident evidence.
rules.name: AiTM Session-Token Theft to Mailbox-Reconnaissance ATO — Cross-Source Stitch
